t: Western Liao adopts dynastic name Great Liao
c: In 1124 the successor state established by Yelü Dashi in the Western Regions also officially adopted the dynastic name Great Liao.

t: Yuwen Xianbei splits into three tribes
c: Following a defeat at the hands of another branch of the Xianbei in 345, the Yuwen split into three tribes, one of which was called the Kumo Xi.

t: Kumo Xi splits, Khitans form
c: In 388 the Kumo Xi itself split, with one group remaining under the name Kumo Xi and the other group becoming the Khitans.

t: Khitans defeated by Northern Qi
c: In 553, the Khitans suffered a defeat to the armies of Northern Qi and lost a large portion of their population as well as cattle.

t: Neiji tribe submits to Tang dynasty
c: The Neiji tribe led by Sun Aocao submitted to the Tang in 619.

t: Ketuyu defeated by Tang; Kumo Xi surrender
c: Ketuyu suffered a defeat against the Tang in 732 and fled while his Kumo Xi allies surrendered to the Tang.

t: Ketuyu defeats Tang army with Turkic allies
c: In 734, Ketuyu defeated a Tang army with the support of his Türkic allies and then lost another battle against Tang forces under the command of Zhang Shougui.

t: Ketuyu's rebellion ends Dahe supremacy
c: The rebellion of Ketuyu ended Dahe supremacy in 730.

t: Khitans become Uighur vassals while paying Tang tribute
c: Following the An Lushan Rebellion, the Khitans became vassals of the Uighurs while simultaneously paying tribute to the Tang, a situation that lasted from 755…

t: Emperor Taizu of Liao born
c: Abaoji, posthumously Emperor Taizu of Liao, was born in 872 to the Yila chieftain, Saladi.

t: Abaoji named supreme Khitan commander
c: In 903, Abaoji was named Yüyue, the supreme commander of all Khitans, second only to the Yaonian Khagan.

t: Abaoji assumes Celestial Emperor title
c: In 916, Abaoji assumed the title of Celestial Emperor, proclaimed a Chinese era name, and built a Confucian temple.

t: Khitan large script developed
c: In 920, Abaoji ordered the development of a Khitan writing system known as the Khitan large script.

t: Raids against Jin and Later Tang
c: From 922 to 923, he raided the Jin and its successor, Later Tang.

t: Bei flees to Later Tang court
c: In 930, Bei fled by sea to the Later Tang court and was received by Li Siyuan as an honoured guest.

t: Shi Jingtang kills rival, founds Later Jin
c: In 937, he was killed by Shi Jingtang, who overthrew Later Tang and ruled Later Jin (Five Dynasties) as a puppet of the Khitans.

t: Taizong campaigns against Tangut tribes
c: In 933, Taizong led a campaign against some Tangut tribes.

t: Later Jin transfers Sixteen Prefectures to Khitans
c: In 938, the puppet emperor of Later Jin transferred the Sixteen Prefectures over to the Khitans, granting them access to the strategic fortifications of…

t: Shi Chonggui revokes Khitan trading privileges
c: In 943, Shi Chonggui revoked the trading privileges of the Khitans in Kaifeng and confiscated their property, sending their representative back to the Khitan…

t: Taizong suffers military defeat in invasion
c: Taizong invaded in the following year but suffered a defeat in 945, having to escape the battle on a camel.

t: Liao assists Northern Han against Later Zhou
c: During Muzong's reign, the Liao assisted Northern Han in fending off an attack by Later Zhou in 952.

t: Yan Po leads Parhae rebellion at Huanglongfu
c: In 975, a Parhae military commander named Yan Po rebelled at Huanglongfu (formerly Buyeo province in Parhae) and killed the director Zhang Ju.

t: Yan Po and Wu Zhaodu invade Tieli
c: Yan Po was still active in 995 when it was reported that he and Wu Zhaodu of Wure invaded Tieli.

t: Buyeo province rebels against Khitans
c: According to a communication between the Song emperor and the king of Jeongan, O Hyŏnmyŏng (Wu Xuanming), in 981, Buyeo province had rebelled against the…

t: Jurchens loot Liao territory
c: The Jurchens looted Liao territory in 973 and 976.

t: Tang Code translated into Khitan language
c: In 983, the Tang Code was ordered to be translated into Khitan for use by the Northern Administration and in 994, it was decided that any Khitan that…

t: Kumo Xi integrated into Khitan administration
c: The Kumo Xi were completely integrated into Khitan administration by 997.

t: Zhongjing established as central capital
c: Their former capital became the "Central Capital" (Zhongjing), which received an inner and outer wall, a Confucian temple, and public buildings were…

t: Emperor Taizong invades Khitan territory
c: In 986, Emperor Taizong of Song conducted a three-pronged invasion and quickly overwhelmed the Khitan border defenses, but the tide turned as they ventured…

t: Li Jiqian submits to Khitans
c: In 986, Li Jiqian of the Tanguts submitted to the Khitans and three later, was given a member of the Khitan imperial family as bride and installed as "King of…

t: Khitans invade Goryeo
c: In 992, the Khitans invaded Goryeo with a large army and made territorial demands along the Yalu River.

t: Khitans and Goryeo begin diplomatic exchanges
c: By 994, regular diplomatic exchanges between the Khitans and Goryeo began.

t: Khitans attack Song dynasty
c: After securing the border with Goryeo, the Khitans attacked the Song dynasty in 994 and laid siege to Zitong, but was repelled by defenders using fire arrows.

t: Kang Cho assassinates Mokjong of Goryeo
c: In 1009, the Goryeo general Kang Cho murdered Mokjong of Goryeo and put Hyeonjong of Goryeo on the throne with the intention of serving as the boy's regent.

t: King Hyeonjong resumes tribute to Khitans
c: In 1020 King Hyeonjong resumed sending tribute and in 1022 the Khitans officially recognized the legitimacy of Hyeonjong's reign.

t: Goryeo and Song conclude peace as equals
c: However, according to historian Bielenstein, Goryeo maintained diplomatic relations with the Song, Hyeonjong kept his own reign title, and the two states…

t: Kingdom of Guiyi sends tribute
c: In 1006, the Kingdom of Guiyi sent tribute to Shengzong's court, which seems to have encouraged him to attack the Ganzhou Uyghur Kingdom.

t: Song expeditions against Ganzhou Uyghurs
c: Expeditions against the Ganzhou Uyghurs were conducted in 1008, 1009, and 1010.

t: Liao defeats Xing Liao and allies
c: In 1030, Xing Liao and its Jurchen and Goryeo allies were defeated by a Liao pincer attack led by Punu.

t: Chinese forbidden from owning bows and arrows
c: In 1043, Chinese living in the Southern Establishments were forbidden from owning bows and arrows.

t: Khitans forbidden from selling slaves to Chinese
c: In 1046, Khitans were forbidden to sell slaves to Chinese.

t: Song bans sacrifice of horses and oxen
c: The army was short on horses so the sacrifice of horses and oxen in ceremonies was banned in 1043.

t: Khitans request territorial concessions from Song
c: In 1042, the Khitans took advantage of the Li Yuanhao's invasion of Song to ask for territorial concessions from the Song.

t: Xingzong refuses to join Li Yuanhao
c: When Li Yuanhao asked the Khitans in 1043 to join him in attacking the Song, Xingzong refused.

t: Xia emperor dies, infant inherits throne
c: In 1048, the Xia emperor died and the throne passed to an infant.

t: Western Xia becomes Song tributary
c: The Western Xia agreed to become a tributary and peaceful relations were restored by 1053.

t: Chinese court dress required at ceremonies
c: In 1055 all officials, and not just the emperor and members of the Southern Establishment, were required to wear Chinese court dress at major ceremonies.

t: Second Guozijian established in Central Capital
c: In 1060, a second Guozijian was set up in the Central Capital in addition to the one in the Supreme Capital.

t: Examination for worthy and good established
c: In 1070 a special palace examination called the "Examination for the worthy and good" (Xianliang ge) was established, requiring entrants to submit 100,000…

t: Bureau for national history established
c: In the same year a bureau for compiling national history was established, which produced in 1085 Veritable Records for the first seven reigns.

t: Daozong undergoes rebirth ceremony
c: In 1067 Daozong underwent a traditional rebirth ceremony, while still engrossed in his studies, to re-establish his legitimacy as leader of the Khitans.

t: Yixin attempts to separate Daozong from Yanxi
c: In 1079, Yixin tried to persuade Daozong to leave Yanxi behind on a hunting trip, which came to the attention of several courtiers who alerted the emperor and…

t: Eastern Capital region hit by flooding
c: In 1074, the Eastern Capital region was hit by severe flooding, after which orders were given to construct flood control works.

t: Goryeo requests territory east of Yalu
c: In 1078 Goryeo's king asked for territory east of the Yalu River, which was rejected without any trouble or break in relations.

t: Metal trade prohibited to Western Xia
c: In 1063, 1064, and 1070, prohibitions were placed on the trade of metals to the Western Xia, Zubu tribes, and Uyghurs.

t: Western Xia requests Khitan attack on Song
c: Between 1103 and 1105, the Western Xia repeatedly requested the Khitans to attack the Song dynasty, but the Liao court refused.

t: Aguda attacks Ningjiang
c: In the late autumn of 1114 Aguda attacked Ningjiang.

t: Jin forces cross Liao River
c: By the end of 1117, Jin forces had crossed the Liao River and conquered several cities.

t: Southern and Western Capitals fall to Jin
c: Both the Southern and Western Capitals fell to the Jin in 1122.

t: Jin capture Tianzuo and imperial family
c: In the early summer of 1123, Dashi was captured by the Jin and forced to lead them to Tianzuo's camp, where the entire imperial family except for Tianzuo and…

t: Tianzuo seeks refuge in Western Xia
c: Tianzuo sought refuge with Emperor Chongzong of Western Xia, who while initially receptive, changed his mind after warnings from the Jurchens and declared…

t: Death of Liao Emperor Tianzuo
c: According to the History of Liao, Tianzuo died at the age of 54 in 1128.

t: Dashi leads Western Liao expansion westward
c: In 1130, Dashi led his host further west in search of new territory.

t: Western Liao defeats Kara-Khanids at Qatwan
c: The new Liao empire expanded to the Aral Sea, defeating the Kara-Khanid Khanate and Seljuk Empire at the Battle of Qatwan in 1141, and establishing their…

t: Kublai blockades Yangtze and besieges Xiangyang
c: From 1268 to 1273, Kublai blockaded the Yangtze River with his navy and besieged Xiangyang, the last obstacle in his way to invading the rich Yangtze River…

t: Mongols conquer Jin dynasty
c: In 1234, the Jin dynasty was conquered by the Mongols, who took control of northern China, maintaining uneasy relations with the Southern Song.

t: Kublai Khan proclaimed Great Khan and founds Yuan
c: His younger brother Kublai Khan was proclaimed the new Great Khan and in 1271 founded the Yuan dynasty.

t: Kublai Khan defeats Song and reunites China
c: After two decades of sporadic warfare, Kublai Khan's armies conquered the Song dynasty in 1279 after defeating the Southern Song in the Battle of Yamen, and…

t: Byzantine embassy arrives in China
c: Chinese records even mention an embassy from the ruler of "Fu lin" (拂菻, i.e. the Byzantine Empire), Michael VII Doukas, and its arrival in 1081.

t: Song commander Guo Kui penetrates Thăng Long
c: After the Vietnamese forces inflicted heavy damages in a raid on Guangxi, the Song commander Guo Kui penetrated as far as Thăng Long (modern Hanoi).

t: Wang Anshi becomes Chancellor of Song
c: After Fan was forced to step down from his office, Wang Anshi became Chancellor of the imperial court.

t: Fang La leads peasant rebellion
c: Later, a peasant rebellion broke out in Zhejiang and Fujian, headed by Fang La in 1120.

t: Song and Jurchens form alliance against Liao
c: The Song official Tong Guan advised Emperor Huizong to form an alliance with the Jurchens, and the joint military campaign under this Alliance Conducted at Sea…

t: Mongol invasions of Vietnam and southern China
c: After the first Mongol invasion of Vietnam in 1258, Mongol general Uriyangkhadai attacked Guangxi from Hanoi as part of a coordinated Mongol attack in 1259…

t: Möngke Khan dies at Diaoyu Castle
c: On August 11, 1259, Möngke Khan died during the siege of Diaoyu Castle in Chongqing.

t: Battle of Yamen crushes Song resistance
c: In the Battle of Yamen on the Pearl River Delta in 1279, the Yuan army, led by the general Zhang Hongfan, finally crushed the Song resistance.

t: Zhu Xi's Four Books becomes civil service examination standard
c: By the year 1241, under the sponsorship of Emperor Lizong, Zhu Xi's Four Books and his commentary on them became standard requirements of study for students…

t: Emperor Zhenzong introduces Champa rice
c: In 1011, Emperor Zhenzong of Song introduced Champa rice to China from Vietnam's Kingdom of Champa, which sent 30,000 bushels as a tribute to Song.

t: Su Song completes horology treatise
c: Su Song was best known for his horology treatise written in 1092, which described and illustrated in great detail his hydraulic-powered, 12 m (39 ft) tall…

t: Qin publishes Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections
c: Qin's major work was the Mathematical Treatise in Nine Sections published in 1247.

t: Hua Sui establishes China's first bronze movable type
c: The wealthy printing patron Hua Sui of the Ming dynasty established China's first metal movable type (using bronze) in 1490.

t: Peking Gazette adopts movable type
c: In 1638, the Peking Gazette switched their printing process from woodblock to movable type printing.

t: Li Jie publishes Yingzao Fashi
c: The architect Li Jie, who published the Yingzao Fashi ('Treatise on Architectural Methods') in 1103, greatly expanded upon the works of Yu Hao and compiled the…

t: Iron Pagoda built during Northern Song
c: Some of the most famous are the Iron Pagoda built in 1049 during the Northern Song and the Liuhe Pagoda built in 1165 during the Southern Song, though there…

t: Liaodi Pagoda constructed in Hebei
c: The tallest is the Liaodi Pagoda built in 1055 in Hebei, towering 84 m (276 ft) in total height.

t: Mongols invade Jin Empire
c: In 1211, the Mongols, led by Genghis Khan, invaded the Jin Empire, winning several victories.

t: Qianlong Emperor commissions history of Manchus
c: In 1778, the Qianlong Emperor reviewed commissioned a new comprehensive history of the Manchus, the Researches on Manchu Origins.

t: Jurchens coalesce into nation-like federation
c: There is no dated evidence of the Jurchens before the time of Wugunai, when the Jurchens began to coalesce into a nation-like federation.

t: Goryeo fails to control Yalu River basin
c: In 984, Goryeo failed to control the Yalu River basin due to conflict with the Jurchens.

t: Goryeo repels Eastern Jurchens stronghold
c: In 1056, Goryeo repelled the Eastern Jurchens and afterward destroyed their stronghold of over 20 villages.

t: Munjong of Goryeo conquers ten villages
c: In 1080, Munjong of Goryeo led a force of 30,000 to conquer ten villages.

t: Wanyan Jurchens reach Chongju
c: In 1104, the Wanyan Jurchens reached Chongju while pursuing tribes resisting them.

t: Nine Fortresses turned over to Wanyan
c: In 1108, Yun Kwan was removed from office and the Nine Fortresses were turned over to the Wanyan clan.

t: King of Goryeo becomes Jin vassal
c: He accepted the Jin demands and in 1126, the king of Goryeo declared himself a Jin vassal (tributary).

t: Liao annexes Balhae
c: With the annexation of Balhae by the Liao in 926, the Jurchens became direct subjects of the Liao.

t: Da Yanlin leads Jurchen rebellion against Liao
c: In 1029, a group of Jurchens joined Da Yanlin, a descendant of Balhae royalty, in rebelling against the Liao dynasty.

t: Aguda elected leader of Jurchens
c: After Wuyashu's death in 1113, his brother Aguda (posthumously Emperor Taizu of Jin) was elected leader of the Jurchens by the tribal elders.

t: Tianzuo crosses Songhua River
c: Tianzuo assembled a massive army west of the Songhua and crossed the river in the winter of 1115.

t: Formal treaty finalized between Jin and Song
c: Despite these diplomatic efforts, by the time a formal treaty was finalized in 1123, Aguda had realized that there was no need for an alliance with the Song…

t: Rebellion against Jin at Eastern Capital
c: In 1119 a rebellion against the Jin occurred at the Eastern Capital and had to be suppressed.
